executiveSummary: Analysis of 21 surveillance reports spanning October 2025 through May 2026 from ECDC and PAHO reveals multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. The most significant concerns include ongoing Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas with persistent zoonotic spillover risk, a resurgent dengue and chikungunya burden across tropical Americas, and the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season coinciding with RSV co-circulation. Pertussis resurging across the Americas and measles importation risks reflect underlying vaccine coverage gaps that warrant urgent public health response.
bottomLine: Multiple simultaneous epidemic threats across the Americas and Europe — including H5N1 zoonotic spillover, dengue surges, pertussis resurgence, and seasonal influenza onset — demand coordinated surveillance intensification and vaccination campaign acceleration.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO updates in November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained H5N1 activity in the Americas
Zoonotic spillover risk to humans from ongoing animal reservoir activity
Dual surveillance alerts spanning over 4 months indicating persistent regional circulation
threats.action: Intensify animal-human interface surveillance, enforce biosafety at poultry and wildlife exposure sites, activate pandemic preparedness protocols, and monitor for human cases with genomic sequencing.

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating elevated dengue burden
Historical context of record-breaking dengue seasons in the Americas in prior years
Co-circulation of Aedes-borne viruses including chikungunya amplifies vector pressure
threats.action: Strengthen Aedes aegypti vector control programs, enhance clinical case detection and serotyping, and ensure healthcare surge capacity in affected countries.

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 signaling active transmission
Co-circulation with dengue in overlapping Aedes vector habitat increases diagnostic challenge
Epidemic alert status suggests transmission exceeding expected baselines
threats.action: Enhance integrated Aedes vector surveillance, ensure differential diagnosis capacity in clinical settings, and issue travel health advisories for affected subregions.

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alert of Southern Hemisphere season start issued April 2026
PAHO alert of simultaneous influenza and RSV co-circulation issued January 2026
ECDC communicable disease threat reports across Weeks 16-20 (April-May 2026) indicating European respiratory virus activity
Dual-pathogen co-circulation increases ICU and hospital burden risk
threats.action: Accelerate Southern Hemisphere influenza vaccination campaigns, monitor RSV severity in vulnerable populations, and ensure hospital surge capacity for dual-pathogen respiratory season.

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO updates in December 2025 and March 2026 indicate sustained and worsening resurgence
Dual-alert cadence over 4 months suggests failure to control initial wave
Resurgence pattern consistent with waning vaccine immunity and coverage gaps
threats.action: Audit national pertussis vaccination coverage, accelerate booster campaigns for adolescents and adults, prioritize vaccination of pregnant women, and enhance laboratory confirmation capacity.

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 indicating active mpox transmission in the Americas
Ongoing circulation following the 2022-2024 global outbreak with potential clade Ib emergence risk
Regional alert status implies transmission above expected endemic levels
threats.action: Strengthen contact tracing and ring vaccination with MVA-BN vaccine, ensure diagnostic PCR availability across member states, and monitor for atypical clinical presentations suggestive of novel clade activity.

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating yellow fever activity in the Americas
Epizootics in non-human primates typically precede human spillover events
Risk of spread to unvaccinated urban populations in historically affected countries
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk departments and municipalities, conduct entomological surveillance for Haemagogus and Sabethes mosquitoes, and investigate any reported primate die-offs.

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 signals measles importation and transmission risk in the Americas
Region previously declared measles-free, making any reintroduction a significant public health threat
Ongoing global measles resurgence creates persistent importation pressure
threats.action: Audit MMR vaccination coverage to ensure ≥95% two-dose coverage, strengthen port-of-entry surveillance, and implement rapid outbreak response protocols for any confirmed cases.

amrSignals: No explicit AMR signals detected in available report titles; however, Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance warrants monitoring given resurgence across the Americas
Avian H5N1 antiviral susceptibility profiling (oseltamivir resistance surveillance) should be conducted on all zoonotic spillover cases
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous co-circulation of multiple arboviruses (dengue, chikungunya) in the Americas suggests heightened Aedes aegypti vector pressure and potential for compounding healthcare burden
Dual pertussis alerts within 4 months indicate a multi-wave resurgence pattern possibly linked to post-COVID pandemic disruption of childhood immunization schedules
Convergence of Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset with RSV activity creates conditions for healthcare system stress similar to the 2022-23 tripledemic pattern
ECDC issuing five consecutive weekly communicable disease threat reports (Weeks 16-20) signals heightened pan-European epidemiological vigilance during spring 2026
Sustained H5N1 alerts across November 2025 and March 2026 in the Americas suggest endemic entrenchment in regional animal reservoirs with persistent pandemic risk window
